entities.summary:
Philonides of Laodicea in Syria, an Epicurean philosopher and mathematician, lived in the Seleucid court during the reigns of Antiochus IV Epiphanes and Demetrius I Soter. He was a prominent figure in the Hellenistic world, known for his contributions to mathematics and his association with the royal court. Philonides' work was influenced by the ideas of Epicurus and his focus on the pursuit of happiness and the avoidance of physical pain.

Philonides was born in Laodicea, a city in the Seleucid Empire, and died in 129 BCE. He was a scholar and a mathematician, and his work had a significant impact on the development of mathematics in the ancient world. Philonides was also known for his association with the royal court, where he likely played a role in the administration of the empire.

Philonides' legacy can be seen in the continued development of mathematics in the ancient world. His work on geometry and arithmetic was widely studied and built upon by later mathematicians. Philonides' association with the royal court also had a lasting impact on the development of the Seleucid Empire.

One of the most striking aspects of Philonides' life is his association with the Seleucid royal family. He was a close friend and advisor to Antiochus IV Epiphanes, who ruled the empire from 175 to 164 BCE. Philonides also played a role in the diplomatic efforts of Demetrius I Soter, who ruled the empire from 162 to 159 BCE.

In conclusion, Philonides of Laodicea was a significant figure in the Hellenistic world, known for his contributions to mathematics and his association with the royal court. His legacy can be seen in the continued development of mathematics in the ancient world and his impact on the development of the Seleucid Empire.
